name: tour
title: Tour
description: A guided tour: a short sequence of steps, each pointing at a part of the page with a title, a sentence and Back, Next and Done.

when: Introducing a screen's main parts to someone new, once, in three to seven steps.
Showing what changed after a redesign, pointing at each moved part.

instead.when: One hint about one control, opened on purpose.
Teaching the first action on an empty screen.
A message that does not point at anything on the page.

guidance.rule: Keep it short: a few steps, a few words of title and one or two sentences each. Nobody reads a tenth step.
Always let people leave. Skip, the close button and Esc call onSkip; Done calls onFinish, so the app can remember which.
Point at things that are on the screen. A target on another route is waited for (targetTimeout), then shown centred or skipped (missingTarget).
The page is dimmed and the target cannot be pressed by default. Use mask={false} for a step that asks people to use the page.

builtIn: Each step is a dialog named by its title and described by its sentence; modal with the default mask (focus stays in the panel, the page is hidden from screen readers), non-modal with mask={false}.
The step's heading takes focus on every step and a status line announces "Step 2 of 5".
Left and Right arrows move between steps, mirrored right to left, and leave text fields alone; Esc skips.
Focus returns to where it was when the tour closes.
With reduced motion the panel and the lit area move without animation and scrolling to a target is instant.
youProvide: A title that says what the step shows, not "Step 1".
A way to start the tour again later (a Help menu item), since a skipped tour is gone.
